name: Tabak Maaz
subtitle: lamb ribs simmered soft in spiced milk, then fried crisp in ghee

ingredients.qty: 800g breast ribs, cut into flat pieces of two or three bones
ingredients.note: ask for the rib rack, not chops
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Ask the butcher for the rib rack cut into flat two- or three-bone pieces about 10cm long. Chops will not do. Tabak maaz is about the flat, crisp-edged slab.
The simmered ribs must cool and dry before they are fried. Cook them a few hours ahead, or the night before, and they will crisp far better.
Have a plate lined with kitchen paper ready; the ribs go straight from the ghee onto it.

steps.text: Put the ribs in a wide pan with the milk, water, turmeric, fennel powder, dry ginger, hing, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf and 1 tsp salt.
Bring to a bare simmer and hold it there, uncovered, for about 60 minutes.
steps.tip: Never let the milk reach a rolling boil. It catches on the base and the whole pot tastes scorched.

steps.text: The ribs are ready when the meat has shrunk back from the bone ends and almost all the liquid has gone, leaving a thick coating.
Lift the ribs onto a rack and leave them to cool and dry for at least 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Frying them wet means spitting ghee and a soggy, pale finish.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy frying pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Fry the ribs in a single layer, 4 minutes on the first side, until the edges are deep gold and audibly crisp.
Turn once and give them 3 minutes on the second side, pressing lightly with a spatula so the whole face colours.
steps.tip: Turn once only. Repeated flipping tears the meat away from the bone.

steps.text: Drain on paper, scatter with salt and the black pepper, and serve hot as a starter with green chutney or plain.

storage: Best eaten within an hour of frying. The simmered, unfried ribs keep 2 days refrigerated in their reduced milk. Fry them to order rather than reheating fried ones.
